info.title: nxs-anomaly native API
info.description: The native /api/v1 contract for nxs-anomaly (API, worker, frontend). This is the authoritative contract; the Grafana-compatibility surface under /api/internal/v1 is a compatibility shim and is NOT part of this contract. The core payloads — user, team, schedule, escalation chain, integration, alert group, alert, notification, delivery attempt — are modelled field by field, with `required` reflecting exactly the keys the engine writes unconditionally; every one still allows additional properties because the underlying storage is JSONB. Remaining resources use the open `Entity` schema. Drift between this document and the router is gated by internal/server/openapi_contract_test.go, and the frontend compiles against types generated from this file (frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts).

get.summary: Stream the alert groups that concern the caller (Server-Sent Events)
get.description: A long-lived text/event-stream for a paired phone or a signed-in person: the app holds it open instead of polling, so an alert reaches the phone in seconds. Events: `hello` (interval and server time), `groups` (the whole current set plus `added`/`changed` since the previous tick; the first one is `baseline: true` and announces nothing), `error` (a read failed; the stream stays open). SSE comments keep it alive between ticks. Not for API keys — there is no "concerns me" for one. Interval: NXS_ANOMALY_MOBILE_STREAM_INTERVAL_SECONDS; concurrent streams are capped by NXS_ANOMALY_MOBILE_STREAM_MAX.

post.summary: Erase a person's data and verify it is gone (admin)
post.description: Credentials, sessions, devices and ChatOps bindings are deleted; the user record, the delivery addresses on their notifications and the actor name/IP on their audit events are pseudonymised. The events themselves are untouched — the record of what happened, including what this person did to other people's data, is what an audit trail exists to keep. The response is a verification rather than a claim: the data is read back and searched for the original identifiers, and the copies outside this database (backups, logs, analytics, traces) are named as out of scope instead of being implied. Idempotent — a second call re-verifies and reports already_erased.

get.summary: Export everything held about one person (admin)
get.description: Assembled by reading the records themselves rather than summarising them. Credentials are reported as present/absent and never included: a password hash is not information about the person, only one more place for it to leak. The two audit sections are bounded by audit_export_limit, which the response states, so a truncated section is visible as truncated. Admin-only despite being a GET.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: Static API key mapped to a role.

bearerAuth.description: Static API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, or a mobile session token (prefix `nxm_`). A mobile session acts as its user, with the role capped at responder.

mobileSession.name: X-Mobile-Session
mobileSession.description: Mobile session token issued by /api/v1/mobile/pairing/redeem (or, administratively, /api/v1/mobile/sessions).

Error.description: The single error envelope used by every failure response.

Entity.description: A domain object stored as a JSON document, for resources this contract does not model field by field. Always carries an `id`; other fields depend on the resource.

source.description: Which layer produced the segment; "" when nobody is on call.

ScheduleSegment.description: One interval of a schedule timeline (engine segmentJSON).

unknown_users.description: Users the schedule names that no longer exist; their slots page nobody.

attached_to.description: Escalation chains that page through this schedule.

acknowledged.description: Every referencing step set allow_uncovered, i.e. the gap is an accepted decision.

ScheduleCoverageItem.description: Only schedules with a gap, a ghost participant or disabled are listed at all.

degraded_attached.description: Degraded schedules an escalation chain actually pages through.

schedules_total.description: Counted after team scoping, like items.

ScheduleOnCall.description: Who is on call for one schedule. user_ids and users are null (not []) when nobody is: the engine builds them with var declarations. `next` is present only when a later segment has a different roster.

exists.description: false when the schedule names a user that no longer exists — a coverage hole, reported rather than hidden.

CurrentOnCall.description: Everyone on call right now across every enabled, in-scope schedule, resolved through Schedule v2 rather than the manual on_duty flag.

webhook_url.description: Incoming-webhook URL of the channel. Empty means command-only: notifications for it are skipped, not delivered. Masked on read paths.

headers.description: Extra request headers sent with every post to webhook_url, e.g. {"Authorization": "env:NXS_ANOMALY_GATEWAY_AUTH"}. Values may be env: references, resolved at send time; the production profile refuses inline values. Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding and Connection cannot be set; at most 16. Values are masked for readers who may not edit configuration.

external_id.description: Channel id on the platform itself (Slack channel id, Telegram chat id); inbound commands name this, not the internal id.

provisioned_by.description: Name of the infrastructure-as-code tool that created this object ("terraform"), absent when a person did. Present means the object is owned by that tool: the API refuses updates and deletes from anyone else, and the web UI disables its own edit controls, because an edit made here would be reverted by the next apply with nothing on screen having said so.

actor.description: The chat handle for inbound, "system" for outbound.

command.description: The command line for inbound; null for outbound.

response.description: An object, not a string: the command result for inbound, {text, alert_group_id} for outbound.

notification_id.description: Outbound only — the notification whose delivery carries the final answer.

delivery_status.description: Outbound only: queued, or skipped_no_transport when the channel has no way to receive.

ChatOpsMessage.description: There is no updated_at: a message is never updated.

flush_at.description: Empty string, never null — the model field is a string.

HistoryItem.description: Every collection here is null rather than [] when empty — they come from var-declared slices and map lookups in the engine.

BulkAcknowledgeResult.description: Each list is null, not [], when nothing fell into it.

step.description: The escalation step kind that would page this person.

pipeline.description: Что сделал пайплайн приёма интеграции: лейблы и заголовок до и после, плюс добавленное, изменённое и удалённое. Отсутствует, если пайплайн не задан.

result.description: Присутствует только когда пайплайн отбросил алерт: dropped_by_pipeline. В этом случае маршрут и предпросмотр не считаются.

RouteDebug.description: Dry-run of an alert against an integration: which route and chain it resolves to and who would be paged. Nothing is delivered. notification_preview is null when the route reaches no chain — the case the readiness routing check calls a blocker.

PagedList.description: Pagination envelope returned by list endpoints whose item type is not modelled.

ReadinessCheck.description: One answerable question about the installation. `blocker` means alerts can be lost or nobody gets paged; `warning` is worth fixing but does not break the alert path. A check that could not run is reported as a blocker, never as a pass.

ReadinessAcknowledgement.description: Who accepted which blockers, and why. `current` is false once the set of blockers has changed since — an acknowledgement covers the problems it was made about, not future ones.

Readiness.description: The readiness report. `ready` means nothing is in the way. `production_ready` is the weaker claim the activation gate uses: either nothing is in the way, or a named person accepted exactly the blockers listed here.

blocker_fingerprint.description: Identifies the exact set of blockers; empty when there are none.

AuthMethods.description: How this deployment expects people to authenticate. Drives the sign-in screen.

oidc_label.description: Issuer host, present only when OIDC is configured, so the button can name the provider.

edition.description: Which edition is running. Present so the sign-in screen can explain a door it cannot draw, rather than quietly drawing one fewer button.

sso_available.description: Whether this build contains the OIDC provider at all. False with oidc=false means the edition has no single sign-on; true with oidc=false means nobody has configured it here.

Identity.description: The principal behind the current request, as the backend sees it. `team_scoped` lets the UI explain an empty list as a boundary rather than as "nothing has happened yet".

locale.description: UI language this person chose. Empty means no choice recorded — the UI then follows the browser. Always empty for a non-user principal.

timezone.description: IANA zone the person's timestamps are rendered in. Empty for a non-user principal, in which case the UI uses the browser zone.

UserPreferences.description: Presentation settings a person owns about themselves. Writable by the person, unlike the rest of the user record.

ActorRef.description: Who performed an action, stored alongside the entity it changed.

PolicyStep.description: One notify/wait step of a personal notification policy (BETA-031).

User.description: A person: both an on-call roster entry and (optionally) an auth principal. Every key here is written unconditionally by CreateUser, so all are required except the opt-in policies.

slack_id.description: Slack account id. Attributes a Slack command or button tap to this person rather than to the bot; empty means the tap runs as the platform service principal.

mattermost_id.description: Mattermost account id. Same role as slack_id, for the Mattermost bot.

locale.description: Chosen UI language; empty means the UI follows the browser.

notification_policies.description: Absent or null means the legacy path: every target fired at once.

role.description: Empty means a roster entry that cannot sign in — the default.

allow_uncovered.description: Accept a schedule with coverage gaps in the next 7 days.

headers.description: TRIGGER_WEBHOOK only: extra request headers sent to webhook_url, with the same rules as ChatOpsChannel.headers. Values are masked for readers who may not edit configuration, and on notifications for everyone.

EscalationChain.description: `steps` is null, not [], for a chain created without any — a draft chain is legal.

Integration.description: An ingest endpoint and its routing. `webhook_secret` is never returned in clear text (an `env:` reference is shown as is); `webhook_secret_set` says whether one is configured. `key` and `routing_key` are masked for roles that cannot edit configuration.

routes.description: Never empty: an integration without routes gets a synthesised default one.

templates.description: Notification text templates keyed by channel name (telegram, email, webhook, sms, phone); the "default" key applies to channels without their own template. Variables: title, severity, reason, group_id, status, user_name, user_username — written as {{ .title }}, {{ title }} or the CamelCase aliases {{ .Title }}, {{ .GroupID }}. An empty object clears all templates and restores the built-in format.

webhook_secret_set.description: Whether an HMAC secret is configured.

provisioned_by.description: Name of the infrastructure-as-code tool that created this object ("terraform"), absent when a person did. Present means the object is owned by that tool: the API refuses updates and deletes from anyone else, and the web UI disables its own edit controls, because an edit made here would be reverted by the next apply with nothing on screen having said so.

pipeline.description: Пайплайн приёма: список этапов, каждый — одно действие (extract, set, rename, remove, gsub, truncate, drop) и необязательное условие if. Выполняется ПОСЛЕ выбора маршрута и до всего остального, поэтому влияет на дедупликацию, сохранённый алерт и текст уведомления, но не на маршрутизацию. См. docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

Report.description: An on-call quality digest (internal/engine/report.go). Generation requires Enterprise with ClickHouse; stored reports remain readable without it. Team-scoped readers cannot access installation-wide reports. required lists the keys Report.toMap() always writes; team_id is null for the installation-wide report. ack/channels/night_load/escalations/noise/late_episodes/exhausted_episodes carry the digest itself.

AlertGroup.description: The required keys are the ones internal/model/alertgroup.go emits unconditionally for every group shape. The optional ones live in the model's Extra map: they are shape-dependent (a direct-paged group has no integration) or nullable state.

Alert.description: One received alert. `alert_group_id` is optional: it is set once the group is resolved, and absent for group-less resolves.

Notification.description: One notification and its delivery state machine (delivery_scheduled → delivered | retry_scheduled → … → failed). `skipped` is terminal: no transport existed for the channel, so nobody was told.

user_id.description: Null for escalation webhooks, which page no particular person.

DeliveryAttempt.description: One provider call: what was tried, what came back (status, code, redacted excerpt) and how long it took. `provider_code` is present only when the protocol has one.

provider_response.description: Redacted provider response; shape depends on the transport.

provider_code.description: Provider response code (HTTP status where the protocol has one).

MaintenanceWindow.description: Planned work on the named integrations. Alert groups those integrations open between starts_at and ends_at are recorded and silenced instead of paging anyone; `integration_ids` always names at least one integration, because an empty list would mean one typo silenced the whole deployment.

provisioned_by.description: Name of the infrastructure-as-code tool that created this object ("terraform"), absent when a person did. Present means the object is owned by that tool: the API refuses updates and deletes from anyone else, and the web UI disables its own edit controls, because an edit made here would be reverted by the next apply with nothing on screen having said so.

Capability.description: One feature and why it is or is not usable here.

state.description: available: present and set up. unavailable_in_edition: this build does not contain it, and no configuration will change that. not_configured: this build contains it and this deployment has not set it up.

detail.description: One sentence a person can act on.

Capabilities.description: What this edition and this deployment can do.

groups_by_status.description: Число групп по статусу — состояние на сейчас, в пределах окна хранения.

groups_by_level.description: Число групп по уровню важности, а не по написанию: high и error попадают в один ключ error.

trend.description: По дню на каждый день диапазона, включая дни без событий.

code.description: One-time code, XXXXX-XXXXX (Crockford base32). Case, spaces and dashes are ignored on redemption.

server_url.description: NXS_ANOMALY_PUBLIC_URL, or empty when it is not set (the UI then uses its own origin).

token.description: The session token. Returned once; only its hash is stored.

expires_at.description: Extended on use; a session unused for 30 days expires.

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description: Column to order by, validated against the collection's own columns; an unknown name is a 400 rather than a silently ignored parameter. Defaults to the newest-first column where the collection has one (alert groups: last_received_at, alerts: received_at, notifications: created_at) and to id elsewhere.

Order.name: order
Order.description: Sort direction. Applies to the requested sort column, or to the collection default when none is named.

Ids.name: ids
Ids.description: Список id через запятую: вернуть только эти элементы. Пустой список возвращает пусто.

reason.description: Why these blockers are acceptable. Required: an acknowledgement without one tells the next person nothing.

at.description: When the backup completed. Defaults to now.

kind.description: Free-form label, e.g. pg_dump or wal-g.

ScheduleOnCall.description: Who is on call for one schedule

CurrentOnCall.description: Who is on call right now
